First, use the special-value evaluation lemma to show that P_{d,r,n}(a,q) has the two a-roots q^{rn} and q^{-rn}; the factor theorem then gives divisibility by (1-aq^{rn})(a-q^{rn}). Second, use the root-of-unity vanishing lemma to show that P_{d,r,n}(a,q) vanishes for every nontrivial nth root of unity in the q-variable; the cyclotomic divisibility lemma then yields divisibility by [n]_q. Since the two factors are coprime, their product divides P_{d,r,n}(a,q). Specializing a=1 identifies the deformed sum with the original theorem sum and turns the factor (1-aq^{rn})(a-q^{rn}) into (1-q^{rn})^2, which contains Φ_n(q)^2 because n divides rn. This gives divisibility of U_{d,n}(q) times the original difference by [n]_q Φ_n(q)^2. Finally, cancel U_{d,n}(q) using its coprimality with the modulus, yielding the exact stated congruence.

assembly_plan.proof_skeleton_nl: Work with the final modulus M_n(q):=[n]_q Φ_n(q)^2, interpreted in the localization-based congruence ring from the shared context so that rational functions with denominators coprime to M_n(q) are legitimate. Define the a-deformed sum S_{d,r,n}(a,q), the target term R_{d,r,n}(q), the harmless clearing factor U_{d,n}(q), and the cleared polynomial P_{d,r,n}(a,q)=a^{n-1}U_{d,n}(q)(S_{d,r,n}(a,q)-R_{d,r,n}(q)). By L2, P_{d,r,n}(a,q) is a polynomial in a with Laurent-polynomial coefficients. By L3, the two special values a=q^{rn} and a=q^{-rn} are roots of P_{d,r,n}(a,q); L4 then yields divisibility by the quadratic factor (1-aq^{rn})(a-q^{rn}). Independently, L5 shows that for every nontrivial nth root of unity ζ, the q-specialization P_{d,r,n}(a,ζ) vanishes identically in a. Since P_{d,r,n}(a,q) is Laurent-polynomial by L2, L6 converts this vanishing into divisibility by [n]_q. Next, L7 proves that [n]_q and (1-aq^{rn})(a-q^{rn}) are coprime in Q[q,q^{-1},a], and L8 combines the two divisibility statements into P_{d,r,n}(a,q) being divisible by [n]_q(1-aq^{rn})(a-q^{rn}). Specializing a=1, L9 identifies P_{d,r,n}(1,q) with U_{d,n}(q)(T_{d,r,n}(q)-R_{d,r,n}(q)) and uses n|rn to upgrade the specialized quadratic factor (1-q^{rn})^2 to Φ_n(q)^2, giving a cleared equality U_{d,n}(q)(T_{d,r,n}(q)-R_{d,r,n}(q))=M_n(q)H_{d,r,n}(q) with H_{d,r,n}(q) Laurent. Finally, L1 shows U_{d,n}(q) is coprime to M_n(q), hence invertible in the localization away from M_n(q), and L10 converts the cleared equality into the desired rational-function congruence T_{d,r,n}(q) ≡ R_{d,r,n}(q) mod M_n(q). Expanding the definitions of T_{d,r,n}(q), R_{d,r,n}(q), and M_n(q) yields exactly the displayed theorem.
